answer: A vertex is where trust actually meets, so it must be triangulated by strangers. An identity needs two holders outside its own vine to anchor its vertex, and one anchor serves one identity, so n aliases need n distinct anchors instead of a single ring. Every anchor is priced by rank: the k-th filing an operator submits costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still requiring unrelated guarantors. An audit re-walks a random edge each epoch, and an unconfirmed edge voids the dune and forfeits every bond on it.
